out_of_band_application_required: change S3 Object Lock default retention from COMPLIANCE/400-day to GOVERNANCE/30-day (bucket-level default affects new objects only)
change lifecycle expiration for current/noncurrent versions from 401 days to 35 days
lower the AWS Budgets monthly guard from USD 8 to USD 5
any already uploaded COMPLIANCE-locked objects (synthetic fixtures and early production artifacts) remain locked until their 400-day retention expires; they are small and cannot be shortened
rationale: The backed-up data is not sensitive and the operator wants storage to expire quickly instead of accumulating for over a year.
S3 API requests are nearly free (PUT USD 0.005/1k, GET/LIST USD 0.0004/1k); the meaningful cost driver is storage growth over the 400-day retention window.
The hourly metrics refresh cuts the dominant S3 LIST/GET poll volume by about 92% versus the 5-minute cadence, with no freshness loss because backup data changes once per night.
Nightly uploads (3 services) and daily restore verification are unchanged; they amount to a few requests per day and preserve the 24-hour RPO target.
caveats: This record is sanitized; no bucket name, account number, access key, KMS identifier, database, token, or player data is included.
GitOps does not mutate AWS; the bucket Object Lock, lifecycle, and Budgets changes must be applied by the out-of-band operator path and re-verified.
GOVERNANCE retains WORM protection for the 30-day window while allowing authorized administrators to clean up older artifacts.
